s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological dysfunction with developmental delay and distinct dysmorphic features
salient_findings: Recurrent episodes of fixed gaze, absence-like loss of contact, and myoclonic-like movements
Developmental delay with gross motor development adequate but fine motor, language, and sociability skills impaired
Distinct dysmorphic features including hypotonic face, high frontal hairline, and epicanthus inversus
key_facts: Age of onset of recurrent episodes: 21 months
Frequency of recurrent episodes: weekly
Duration of episodes: from a few seconds to 15 minutes
Family history of intellectual disability and epilepsy
Normal tonus and reflexes on physical examination
Mild psychomotor delay
Broad-based gait
Normal routine hematological, biochemical, and thyroid tests
Mild frontal colpocephaly on brain MRI
Normal sleep-deprived electroencephalogram (EEG)
Mild hyperopia, intermittent strabismus, and nystagmus of congenital origin on ophthalmological examination
Pathogenic nonsense variant in the CHD2 gene detected by Clinical Exome Sequencing

shortlist.label: CDKL5 disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological dysfunction, developmental delay, and seizures

shortlist.label: PME syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Myoclonic-like movements and epilepsy in the context of developmental delay

shortlist.label: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological dysfunction, developmental delay, and seizures

shortlist.label: Myoclonic astatic epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: Myoclonic-like movements and epilepsy in the context of developmental delay

shortlist.label: Dravet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological dysfunction, developmental delay, and seizures

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent episodes of fixed gaze, absence-like loss of contact, myoclonic-like movements, and frequent falls, along with a family history of intellectual disability and epilepsy, are consistent with myoclonic astatic epilepsy. The normal EEG and presence of myoclonic-like movements also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: CDKL5 disorder
rejected.why: Typically associated with more severe developmental delay and earlier onset of seizures

rejected.label: PME syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by progressive myoclonus epilepsy, which is not the primary presentation in this case

rejected.label: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with multiple seizure types, including atonic, tonic, and atypical absences, which are not all present in this case

rejected.label: Dravet syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with febrile seizures and a more severe clinical course, which is not consistent with this patient's presentation
